name: Trish Millines Dziko
milestone_by_age_26: No material, field-defining milestone by age 26 found. Graduated Monmouth with BS CS in 1979 (age ~22) and took ordinary early industry roles; major visibility came later at Microsoft (joined 1988, age ~31) and co-founding Technology Access Foundation in 1996 (age ~39).
early_history_summary: Born 1957 and raised in New Jersey by adoptive single mother Pat Millines; became first woman with a full basketball scholarship at Monmouth College and first in her family to graduate college (BS Computer Science, 1979). Early career included Computer Sciences Corporation testing military radar software and Telecalc in Seattle; later spent ~9 years at Microsoft including diversity administration, then left in 1996 to co-found TAF with Jill Hull.
family_context_summary: Adopted and raised in New Jersey by single mother Pat Millines; first in family to attend college. Mother died of cancer about a month before Dziko's high school graduation.
parent_family_domain_summary: Mother emphasized college education; no documented tech-domain parental expertise.
evidence_summary: Birth year 1957 is documented. College graduation and first software jobs by ~22 are ordinary early-career steps, not independently notable breakthroughs. Documented material impact—Microsoft diversity work, BAM, and TAF/STEMbyTAF—occurred well after age 26. Family hardship (mother's death senior year of high school) is documented but does not create an age-26 career milestone under the rubric.

name: Sarah Allen
milestone_by_age_26: No confirmed birth year found in reviewed sources, so age at co-founding CoSA (1990) and related After Effects/Shockwave work cannot be verified as ≤26. Year of birth is missing on Wikipedia; without it a material age-26 milestone cannot be established.
early_history_summary: Attended Brown University in computer science and visual arts. Shortly after college in 1990 she co-founded CoSA (Company of Science and Art), which originated After Effects (acquired into Adobe); later led Shockwave Multiuser Server, Flash Media Server, and Flash Video work, co-founded Blazing Cloud and Mightyverse, and was a 2013 Presidential Innovation Fellow at the Smithsonian.
evidence_summary: Career milestones including CoSA/After Effects and Shockwave/Flash are well documented, but Wikipedia and secondary profiles mark birth year as missing. Without a dated birth year, eligibility by age 26 cannot be confirmed under the strict rule. Later recognition (Top 25 Women of the Web 1998; PIF 2013) also lacks age anchors.

name: Jessica Powell
category: Tech executive / communications (former Google VP) / AudioShake founder
milestone_by_age_26: No Wikipedia page and no confirmed birth year or dated material milestone at age ≤26 found. Public profile centers on later-career Google VP of Communications role and post-Google founding of AudioShake; early career timing is not verifiably age-bounded.
early_history_summary: Former Vice President of Communications at Google (global PR/communications leadership; also associated with Maps/local and management-team-level roles in coverage). Later co-founded AudioShake, an AI sound-separation company, and authored the tech satire novel The Big Disruption. Public bios emphasize multi-year Google tenure rather than a dated breakout before 26.
evidence_summary: No birth year, no Wikipedia biography, and no second-source dated youthful milestone (founding, award, product breakout) by age 26 were located. Google leadership and AudioShake founding appear mid/late career. Cannot establish age_26_eligible under the strict rule.

name: Frederic Lardinois
milestone_by_age_26: No Wikipedia page and no confirmed birth year found. Long-running tech writing career (SiliconFilter, ReadWriteWeb, TechCrunch from ~2012, later The New Stack) is not anchored to a dated material milestone verifiably achieved at age ≤26.
early_history_summary: Tech writer and editor known for covering startups, cloud, and AI. Founded SiliconFilter, wrote for ReadWriteWeb, joined TechCrunch around 2012 and stayed through ~2025, then became Senior Editor for AI at The New Stack. Public profiles emphasize byline history rather than an early breakout event.
evidence_summary: Without birth year or a clearly dated age-bounded achievement (e.g., founding a major outlet or winning a field-defining award by 26), eligibility cannot be established. Tech journalism career success appears cumulative and post-early-20s in available sources.

name: Kurt Bollacker
milestone_by_age_26: No confirmed birth year found (Wikipedia marks year of birth missing). Co-created CiteSeer (papers ~1998 while visiting NEC Research Institute) and later Freebase/Metaweb and Internet Archive Wayback work; without birth year, age at those milestones cannot be verified as ≤26.
early_history_summary: Ph.D. in Computer Engineering from UT Austin; earlier biomedical research engineering at Duke on electro-cardiography (papers early 1990s). Co-created CiteSeer with Steve Lawrence and C. Lee Giles; later Technical Director at Internet Archive (Wayback Machine), Chief Scientist at Metaweb (Freebase), and Digital Research Director at the Long Now Foundation; Common Crawl advisory board.
evidence_summary: CiteSeer (~1998) and Freebase (~2000s) are material contributions, but birth year is undocumented. PhD timing and 1991–1995 biomedical publications suggest graduate-level work that may or may not fall at ≤26; without a birth date the strict rule requires ineligible.

name: Greg Maxwell
category: Bitcoin Core developer / cryptographer / open-source engineer
milestone_by_age_26: No Wikipedia page and no confirmed birth year found. Documented Bitcoin Core contributions begin ~2011 (commit access 2012), Blockstream co-founding mid-2010s, and earlier Opus/codec and cypherpunk work; none can be age-verified as ≤26 without birth year. Self-description of politically coming of age in the early 1990s implies he was likely well over 26 by Bitcoin prominence.
early_history_summary: Independent researcher and free-software developer; early Wikipedia contributor and Mozilla/Opus audio codec contributor; involved with Hal Finney's RPOW in the mid-2000s; became major Bitcoin Core developer from 2011–2018 (CoinJoin, protocol review, SegWit-era work) and co-founded Blockstream, later stepping back from day-to-day Bitcoin roles.
evidence_summary: Field impact is high but arrives via adult open-source and crypto work without a public birth year. Bitcoin and Blockstream milestones are almost certainly post-26 given mid-2000s prior cypherpunk activity and early-1990s political coming-of-age remarks. Strict eligibility fails without dated age proof.

name: Danny Crichton
milestone_by_age_26: No Wikipedia page and no confirmed birth year found. Stanford graduation, Fulbright in South Korea, early VC roles, and TechCrunch managing editorship are documented but not age-dated to ≤26; no material breakout milestone with two-source age confirmation by 26.
early_history_summary: Stanford B.S. in Mathematical and Computational Sciences (honors, Firestone Medal thesis); Fulbright research on Korean startup industrial policy at KAIST; early-stage investor at General Catalyst and CRV; TechCrunch managing editor and Seoul-based correspondent; later Partner, Research at Lux Capital and Manhattan Institute fellow.
evidence_summary: Career is substantial but lacks a birth year and lacks a clearly exceptional, dated ≤26 milestone (elite undergrad alone is not sufficient under the rubric). TechCrunch leadership and Lux partnership are later-career roles. Marked ineligible.

name: Michael L. Kazar
milestone_by_age_26: No confirmed birth year found (Wikipedia marks year of birth missing). Co-created Andrew File System at CMU and earned a 1985 CMU Ph.D.; later co-founded Transarc (1989), Spinnaker, and Avere Systems. Without birth year, age at AFS/Ph.D. work cannot be verified as ≤26.
early_history_summary: BS Mathematics and BS EECS from MIT; Ph.D. Computer Science from Carnegie Mellon (1985 thesis on automatic distribution of programs and data). Core AFS designer; Transarc co-founder commercializing AFS (IBM acquired 1994); later CTO roles at Spinnaker Networks (sold to NetApp) and Avere Systems; 2013 IEEE Reynold B. Johnson Award and 2016 ACM Software System Award for AFS.
evidence_summary: AFS is a material systems milestone and peers such as Sherri Nichols have documented age-26 eligibility for related work, but Kazar himself has no public birth year. Ph.D. year 1985 and Transarc founding 1989 cannot be age-mapped. Strict rule requires ineligible.

early_history_summary: Batch points to https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Black, which is a rugby scrum-half (NRL/English Championship), not a technology figure. evidence_summary: Identity mismatch prevents coding a tech trajectory. Without a confirmed person, birth year, and two-source age-26 milestone, eligibility fails. Rugby debut at age ~20 is outside the founder/engineer research frame and was not the intended candidate.

name: James P. Anderson Jr.
milestone_by_age_26: Born 1930; first computing job at Univac in 1956 (age ~26) was ordinary early employment, not a field-defining milestone. Landmark contributions—D-825 multiprocessor work (~1962, age ~32), the 1972 Anderson Report/reference monitor, and 1980 intrusion-detection report—all occurred well after age 26.
early_history_summary: Born Easton, Pennsylvania; Penn State meteorology degree; U.S. Navy gunnery/radio officer 1953–1956, where cryptography interest began. Hired by John Mauchly at Univac (1956), then Burroughs Advanced Systems (1959), Auerbach (1964–66), then founded James P. Anderson Company (1966) as long-running security consultant. Authored foundational computer security planning and intrusion-detection reports for U.S. government.
family_context_summary: Born in Easton, Pennsylvania; family financial/domain details not documented in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Birth year 1930 and career timeline are solidly sourced. Navy service and first programming job by 26 do not meet the material-milestone bar used for age_26_eligible. Fame and foundational influence in information security arrived in the 1960s–1980s. Deceased 2007.

name: Timothy Canham
category: NASA JPL software engineer (Ingenuity Mars helicopter)
milestone_by_age_26: No confirmed birth year found. Graduated Clarkson University in 1991 and spent career at JPL; fame for Ingenuity software/operations leadership (first powered extraterrestrial flight, 2021) is clearly mid/late-career. No dated material milestone verifiably at age ≤26.
early_history_summary: Grew up area of Rushville, NY (Marcus Whitman High School); Clarkson B.S. electrical and computer engineering (1991). Longtime JPL engineer; contributed to Curiosity landing software; architect of Fprime flight software framework; software then operations lead for Ingenuity Mars Helicopter (prototype work from ~2015; flight 2021). Team awards include Swigert Award and Collier Trophy.
evidence_summary: Ingenuity is a historic engineering achievement but occurred decades after a 1991 bachelor's degree. Without birth year, even early JPL employment cannot be age-checked; ordinary post-grad hiring is not itself a material age-26 breakout under the rubric.

name: Mikhail Atallah
category: Computer scientist (algorithms, security) / professor / Arxan co-founder
milestone_by_age_26: No confirmed birth year found. B.S. American University of Beirut 1975, M.S. 1980 and Ph.D. 1982 from Johns Hopkins under S. Rao Kosaraju, then Purdue faculty from 1982; NSF Presidential Young Investigator 1985; Arxan co-founded 2001. Even under typical age assumptions, Ph.D./faculty milestones land near or after 26 and cannot be verified ≤26 without birth year.
early_history_summary: Lebanese-American computer scientist; AUB bachelor's (1975), Johns Hopkins MS/PhD (1980/1982) in parallel algorithms; continuous Purdue CS faculty career becoming distinguished professor. Research spans parallel/dynamic computational geometry, string algorithms, and later computer security (text watermarking, software anti-tamper). Co-founded Arxan Technologies (anti-piracy/anti-tamper); ACM Fellow (2006) and IEEE Fellow (since 1997).
evidence_summary: Strong academic career with PYI and society fellowships, but birth year missing and signature security/entrepreneurship milestones are post-early-career. B.S. alone is not a material breakout. Ineligible under strict age-26 rule.
